title: run-acceptance.v1
description: The early response the input-to-outcome lifecycle needs: a run identity issued at admission, before the outcome exists. The deployed pilot is synchronous and its completion response cannot acknowledge a run early enough for the dialog handoff, so this protocol is proposed work sitting in front of that validated execution boundary — not a description of what the service does today.

disposition.description: ADMITTED issues a runId. REFUSED preserves the draft and states why. UNCERTAIN means delivery could not be established: the request is retained for reconciliation and is never automatically resubmitted.

runId.description: Present only when ADMITTED. Persisted against requestId before any external effect begins, which is what makes a repeat safe.

deduplicated.description: True when this requestId already had a run. The same runId is returned; nothing executes a second time.

selection.description: What the server resolved the command to. Echoed so the workbench can show which authority actually ran, and pin the outcome to it.

refusal.description: Why a request was refused. Distinct codes matter: a stale publication, an unavailable provider, a refused input and a domain failure are different facts and are never collapsed into one error.
